title: CDL hours of service practice questions
description: Free CDL hours of service practice questions on 49 CFR Part 395. Every answer is explained and linked to the section it comes from.

questions.question: How does 395.2 define driving time?

options.A: All time from reporting for work until being released from work
options.B: All time spent at the driving controls of a commercial motor vehicle in operation
options.C: All time the vehicle's engine is running, whether or not the vehicle moves
options.D: All time the driver is on board while the vehicle is moving, in any seat

questions.explanation: 395.2: "Driving time means all time spent at the driving controls of a commercial motor vehicle in operation."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.2, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Driving time means all time spent at the driving controls of a commercial motor vehicle in operation.

questions.question: Under the on-duty time definition in 395.2, how is time spent loading or unloading a commercial motor vehicle, or supervising or assisting in the loading or unloading, counted?

options.C: As driving time
options.D: As on-duty time

questions.explanation: The 395.2 list of what "On-duty time shall include" covers "All time loading or unloading a commercial motor vehicle, supervising, or assisting in the loading or unloading".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.2, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: On-duty time shall include: [...] (5) All time loading or unloading a commercial motor vehicle, supervising, or assisting in the loading or unloading, attending a commercial motor vehicle being loaded or unloaded,

questions.question: Which passenger-seat time does the 395.2 definition of on-duty time leave out of on-duty time?

options.A: Up to 3 hours riding in the passenger seat of a property-carrying vehicle moving on the highway immediately before or after a period of at least 7 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth
options.B: Any amount of time riding in the passenger seat of any moving commercial motor vehicle
options.C: Up to 5 hours riding in the passenger seat after any off-duty period of at least 2 hours
options.D: Up to 3 hours riding in the passenger seat of a passenger-carrying vehicle at any time of day

questions.explanation: On-duty time includes all time in or on a commercial motor vehicle other than, among others, "Up to 3 hours riding in the passenger seat of a property-carrying vehicle moving on the highway immediately before or after a period of at least 7 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.2, Definitions (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: All time in or on a commercial motor vehicle, other than: [...] (iii) Up to 3 hours riding in the passenger seat of a property-carrying vehicle moving on the highway immediately before or after a period of at least 7 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth;

questions.question: What limit on total driving time does 395.3(a)(3)(i) set for a property-carrying driver during the 14-hour period that follows 10 consecutive hours off duty?

options.C: 11 hours
options.D: 18 hours

questions.explanation: 395.3(a)(3)(i): "A driver may drive a total of 11 hours during the period specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.3, Maximum driving time for property-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Driving time. A driver may drive a total of 11 hours during the period specified in paragraph (a)(2) of this section.

questions.question: What does 395.3(a)(1) require of a property-carrying driver before driving at the start of a work shift?

options.C: 10 consecutive hours off duty
options.D: 10 hours off duty in total, split into any number of breaks

questions.explanation: 395.3(a)(1): "A driver may not drive without first taking 10 consecutive hours off duty".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.3, Maximum driving time for property-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Start of work shift. A driver may not drive without first taking 10 consecutive hours off duty;

questions.question: What period does 395.3(a)(2) set, after which a property-carrying driver may not drive?

options.A: 14 consecutive hours after coming on-duty following 10 consecutive hours off-duty
options.B: 17 consecutive hours after coming on-duty following 10 consecutive hours off-duty
options.C: 18 consecutive hours after coming on-duty following 10 consecutive hours off-duty
options.D: 24 consecutive hours after coming on duty, with no off-duty requirement

questions.explanation: 395.3(a)(2): "A driver may not drive after a period of 14 consecutive hours after coming on-duty following 10 consecutive hours off-duty."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.3, Maximum driving time for property-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: 14-hour period. A driver may not drive after a period of 14 consecutive hours after coming on-duty following 10 consecutive hours off-duty.

questions.question: Under 395.3(a)(3)(ii), driving is not permitted once more than how many hours of driving time have passed without at least a consecutive 30-minute interruption in driving status (for drivers not covered by an exception in 395.1)?

options.C: 11 hours
options.D: 8 hours

questions.explanation: Except for qualifying short-haul drivers, "driving is not permitted if more than 8 hours of driving time have passed without at least a consecutive 30-minute interruption in driving status."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.3, Maximum driving time for property-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Except for drivers who qualify for either of the short-haul exceptions in § 395.1(e)(1) or (2), driving is not permitted if more than 8 hours of driving time have passed without at least a consecutive 30-minute interruption in driving status.

questions.question: Under 395.3(b)(2), what limit applies to a property-carrying driver whose employing motor carrier operates commercial motor vehicles every day of the week?

options.A: No driving after having been on duty 75 hours in any period of 8 consecutive days
options.B: No driving after having been on duty 70 hours in any period of 8 consecutive days
options.C: No driving after having been on duty 84 hours in any period of 8 consecutive days
options.D: No driving after having been on duty 70 hours in any period of 10 consecutive days

questions.explanation: The driver may not drive after "Having been on duty 70 hours in any period of 8 consecutive days if the employing motor carrier operates commercial motor vehicles every day of the week."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.3, Maximum driving time for property-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Having been on duty 70 hours in any period of 8 consecutive days if the employing motor carrier operates commercial motor vehicles every day of the week.

questions.question: Under 395.3(c), what may end a period of 7 or 8 consecutive days for a property-carrying driver?

options.A: The beginning of an off-duty period of 34 or more consecutive hours
options.B: Any off-duty period of 10 or more consecutive hours
options.C: Any off-duty period of 30 or more consecutive hours
options.D: Two separate off-duty periods that total 34 hours

questions.explanation: 395.3(c): "Any period of 7 consecutive days may end with the beginning of an off-duty period of 34 or more consecutive hours." The same applies to any period of 8 consecutive days.

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.3, Maximum driving time for property-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (1) Any period of 7 consecutive days may end with the beginning of an off-duty period of 34 or more consecutive hours. (2) Any period of 8 consecutive days may end with the beginning of an off-duty period of 34 or more consecutive hours.

questions.question: What limit on driving time following 8 consecutive hours off duty does 395.5(a)(1) set for a passenger-carrying driver?

options.C: 10 hours
options.D: 16 hours

questions.explanation: No driver shall drive a passenger-carrying commercial motor vehicle "More than 10 hours following 8 consecutive hours off duty".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.5, Maximum driving time for passenger-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (1) More than 10 hours following 8 consecutive hours off duty; or

questions.question: What on-duty limit following 8 consecutive hours off duty does 395.5(a)(2) set, after which a passenger-carrying driver may not drive for any period?

options.C: 24 hours
options.D: 19 hours

questions.explanation: 395.5(a)(2) bars driving "For any period after having been on duty 15 hours following 8 consecutive hours off duty."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.5, Maximum driving time for passenger-carrying vehicles (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (2) For any period after having been on duty 15 hours following 8 consecutive hours off duty.

questions.question: When a property-carrying driver uses the two-period sleeper berth option in 395.1(g)(1)(ii), what does the rule require of one of the two rest periods?

options.A: At least 5 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth
options.B: At least 6 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth
options.C: At least 4 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth
options.D: At least 7 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth

questions.explanation: 395.1(g)(1)(ii)(B): "One rest period is at least 7 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.1, Scope of rules in this part (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (B) One rest period is at least 7 consecutive hours in the sleeper berth;

questions.question: What minimum length does 395.1(g)(1)(ii)(A) set for each of the two rest periods in a property-carrying sleeper berth split?

options.C: 15 consecutive minutes
options.D: 2 consecutive hours

questions.explanation: 395.1(g)(1)(ii)(A): "Neither rest period is shorter than 2 consecutive hours".

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.1, Scope of rules in this part (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: (A) Neither rest period is shorter than 2 consecutive hours;

questions.question: Under 395.1(g)(1)(iii)(B), how do qualifying split sleeper berth rest periods affect the 14-hour driving window in 395.3(a)(2)?

options.A: The 14-hour driving window does not include them
options.B: They are counted in full toward the 14-hour window
options.C: They extend the 14-hour window to 16 hours
options.D: They restart the 60- and 70-hour limits

questions.explanation: 395.1(g)(1)(iii)(B): "The 14-hour driving window for purposes of § 395.3(a)(2) does not include qualifying rest periods under paragraph (g)(1)(ii) of this section."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.1, Scope of rules in this part (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The 14-hour driving window for purposes of § 395.3(a)(2) does not include qualifying rest periods under paragraph (g)(1)(ii) of this section.

questions.question: Outside the separate Alaska provision, what limit does 395.1(b)(1) set on extra driving for a driver who meets adverse driving conditions and cannot, because of them, safely complete the run within the normal maximum?

options.C: Not more than two additional hours
options.D: Not more than 5 additional hours

questions.explanation: The driver may drive "for not more than two additional hours beyond the maximum allowable hours permitted under § 395.3(a) or § 395.5(a) to complete that run or to reach a place offering safety for the occupants of the commercial motor vehicle and security for the commercial motor vehicle and its cargo."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.1, Scope of rules in this part (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: Except as provided in paragraph (h)(3) of this section, a driver who encounters adverse driving conditions, as defined in § 395.2, and cannot, because of those conditions, safely complete the run within the maximum driving time or duty time during which driving is permitted under § 395.3(a) or § 395.5(a) may drive and be permitted or required to drive a commercial motor vehicle for not more than two additional hours beyond the maximum allowable hours permitted under § 395.3(a) or § 395.5(a) to complete that run or to reach a place offering safety for the occupants of the commercial motor vehicle and security for the commercial motor vehicle and its cargo.

questions.topic: Records of duty status and ELDs
questions.question: What retention period does 395.8(k)(1) set for a motor carrier's records of duty status and supporting documents for each of its drivers?

options.A: 30 days from the date of receipt
options.B: 3 months from the date of receipt
options.C: 7 days from the date of receipt
options.D: Not less than 6 months from the date of receipt

questions.explanation: "A motor carrier shall retain records of duty status and supporting documents required under this part for each of its drivers for a period of not less than 6 months from the date of receipt."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.8, Driver's record of duty status (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: A motor carrier shall retain records of duty status and supporting documents required under this part for each of its drivers for a period of not less than 6 months from the date of receipt.

questions.topic: Records of duty status and ELDs
questions.question: Under 395.8(k)(2), which records of duty status must a driver have in their possession and available for inspection while on duty?

options.A: Only the record for the current day
options.B: A copy for the previous 3 consecutive days
options.C: A copy of each record for the previous 7 consecutive days
options.D: Only the records the motor carrier has not yet received

questions.explanation: "The driver shall retain a copy of each record of duty status for the previous 7 consecutive days which shall be in his/her possession and available for inspection while on duty."

source.title: eCFR: 49 CFR 395.8, Driver's record of duty status (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.evidence: The driver shall retain a copy of each record of duty status for the previous 7 consecutive days which shall be in his/her possession and available for inspection while on duty.

options.C: 10 days
options.D: 15 days

questions.explanation: One listed case is operating "In a manner requiring completion of a record of duty status on not more than 8 days within any 30-day period".
